trials.name: INTERCEPT-AD
trials.drug: ACU193 / sabirnetug (monoclonal antibody targeting amyloid-beta oligomers)
trials.population: Adults aged 55-90 with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) due to AD or mild AD
trials.primary_endpoint: Incidence and Nature of Treatment-Related Adverse Events (AE) or Serious Adverse Events (SAE)
trials.results_summary: Sabirnetug was generally well tolerated with dose-proportional exposure and central target engagement (binding to Aβ oligomers in CSF). Higher doses demonstrated a 20-25% reduction in amyloid plaques over three months, with mild-to-moderate ARIA-E occurring in 5 of 48 treated participants.

evidence_assessment: Sabirnetug (ACU193) is an investigational monoclonal antibody uniquely targeting amyloid-beta oligomers, currently being evaluated for clinical efficacy in early Alzheimer's disease in the Phase 2 ALTITUDE-AD trial (NCT06335173). The clinical evidence base relies entirely on the completed Phase 1 INTERCEPT-AD trial (NCT04931459), which established initial safety, pharmacokinetics, and evidence of central target engagement—including a modest reduction in amyloid plaques at higher doses over a short duration. However, because no Phase 2 or Phase 3 efficacy readouts are yet available, the clinical benefit of sabirnetug in slowing cognitive and functional decline remains strictly unproven. The Alzheimer's field awaits the readout of ALTITUDE-AD in late 2026 to determine if targeting Aβ oligomers selectively translates to meaningful clinical outcomes.
discrepancies: No major discrepancies. The document correctly describes ALTITUDE-AD as an 'ongoing' Phase 2 trial of 542 participants; the registry provides slightly more precision, confirming that the study has reached its full actual enrollment of 542 and its status is now formally 'Active, not recruiting'.
